messages.subject: What to do about multinomial...
messages.body_plain:
I spent the last couple of days going through the recent changes to gbm. It seems the big issue is multinomial. I see throughout the package special code carved out just for multinomial. That makes it very hard to maintain. Add to this the issues of segfaults with multinomial, plots not working with multinomial, and I'm not sure if any of the active developers were involved with the multinomial implementation.

So... I have a proposal. What would you all think about removing the multinomial functionality from gbm? At the same time we can fork the current package into a new "gbmmulti" package with the idea that it would be developed into a package just for multinomial. The multinomial algorithm is really quite unique and doesn't really merge well with the models involving univariate outcomes.

The alternative would be to engage the multinomial developer... (Harry, do you know who that was?)... and try to fix it.

Thoughts?

Greg

messages.body_plain:
[resending to mailing list because I'm incompetent]

+1

I have been putting off writing a very similar email for a couple of months.

We probably need to agree a roadmap for the next few versions of gbm.  I'm thinking that we want 2.2 to be the closest point to where we are now that we think to be actually correct and maintainable.

That, in my mind, would remove multinomial, and might also end up refactoring the R code into glm-style `family' objects.

We might be able to revisit multinomial once we've made those tidies, but I think that could be a few versions away.

pdm

messages.subject: Family interface
messages.body_plain:
So what do you all mean by going with the family interface? I'm familiar with the glm implementation, but it defines all the links and derivatives within the family object in R. In gbm I implemented it all in C++ for speed. Are you proposing to move all the deviance, fit best constant, get initial fit functions into R? That seems like something that would be nice for the user interface but costly for computation time.

Greg

messages.subject: Re: Family interface
messages.body_plain:
Can I suggest that we postpone any changes to the family/distribution parameters? I'm not quite sure what problem it aims to solve. Perhaps to make it easier to add new loss functions? Make gbm look more like glm? Both noble causes, but I don't get any complaints about the current style.

So can we agree on the following?
1. Fork the current code to a new project "gbmmulti"
2. Add notes that it is intended to be a separate project just for multinomial gbm if someone out there wishes to adopt it.
3. Strip multinomial from gbm (is there a way to check whether any other R package depends on gbm multinomial? Give those package authors some forewarning?)
4. Run checks, make sure everything is working, passes test suite, etc.
5. Post new version to CRAN

Greg
